This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.195/2023 registered at Police Station - Bada Malehra, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 07.10.2023.

2. As per the prosecution story, in short, is that in the year 2019, prosecutrix aged about 17 years,
went to Delhi along with her father to attend the marriage function at their relatives place.
Where she met with the applicant, he allured her and committed the coffence, on her protest applicant threatened her to dire consequences.
Thereafter, when she returned to her village Darguwa in the year 2022, applicant made physical relations with the prosecutrix various times.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is further submitted that in the year 2019, prosecutrix herself developed physical relationship with the present applicant.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that she herself went with the applicant in different places but she never complained to anyone.
Thereafter FIR was lodged by her belatedly i.e. on 04.09.2023.
It is further submitted that charge-sheet has been filed.
There is no criminal case registered against the present applicant.
Applicant is in custody since 07.10.2023.

Trial would take considerable time,
therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be granted bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submits that at the time of the incident prosecutrix was minor and aged about 17 years.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code o f Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
In case of breach of any of the aforementioned conditions, the bail granted by this Court shall stand rejected automatically.
7 . This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE MTK Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141252694/
